sections.lead: We connect LINE Official Accounts to monday.com, HubSpot and your ERP, so a friend-add becomes a contact record with consent attached, and the conversation stops ending at the Official Account Manager.

head.heading: LINE keeps nothing for you.
head.lead: LINE gives you a display name, an icon, a status message and a language. It will not give you a phone number, an email address or a way to re-read a message you failed to store. Everything a CRM needs, you have to capture yourself. That is the whole engineering problem, and it is why LINE projects that start as "just connect the chat tool" end up rebuilt. We design the persistence and consent layer first, because LINE keeps no logs for you and will not hand the data back.

head.lead: Several of these cannot be retrofitted. Getting them wrong at the start means rebuilding, not patching. LINE declines to publish a retention period for media content, so we do not quote one.

items.body: A client already running a vendor chat tool on their OA cannot simply add a second integration. The module-channel escape hatch is gated behind a corporate application.

sections.heading: Viber has no CRM app. *We build the one you need.*
sections.lead: Rakuten Viber publishes no integration for monday.com, HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho or Dynamics. The channel has simply never been productised. That is the whole problem, and the whole opportunity: we build the path so Viber behaves like a first-class channel in the system you already run.

head.heading: Where customers are, and no connector exists.
head.lead: In the Philippines, Greece, Bulgaria, Serbia and Ukraine, Viber is where customers actually are. It is also the least served channel in enterprise software: no first-party CRM app anywhere, no Make app, no Zapier app, no n8n node. There are good technical reasons for that, and they are the reason this work is worth doing properly rather than improvising it.

head.heading: Facts that decide *whether Viber is viable for you at all.*
head.lead: We would rather tell you this before you commit than after. On two of these rows the honest answer is sometimes “not this channel”. Rates and rules from Rakuten Viber’s published documentation and EUR rate cards, retrieved September 2026. The rate cards carry no version date, so we re-retrieve them before quoting.

items.body: Domestic rates apply only when your entity is headquartered in the recipient’s country. In the Philippines that is the difference between roughly €0.0026 and €0.0750 per message, decided by where you are incorporated, not by how you send.
items.label: Domestic vs international
items.title: A legal-entity test, not a routing test

items.body: Viber’s own help centre lists chats with bots among the communications that are not end-to-end encrypted. Several aggregators claim otherwise. If you are regulated, design around the documented position.
items.label: Encryption
items.title: Business messaging is not end-to-end encrypted

items.body: Its business terms disclaim any representation that the service meets the needs of entities handling personal health information or data on children. For clinical use cases we will usually point you elsewhere.
items.label: Regulated sectors
items.title: Viber warrants nothing for health data

items.body: Onboarding needs a warranty letter, a service qualification form, a non-promotional example message and six logo sizes. Viber issues a Service ID in two to three days. There is no self-serve path.
items.label: Access
items.title: Approved partner only, and Viber approves the sender

items.body: Once a subscriber messages you, everything inside the session is free. A conversational design costs a flat monthly bot fee and very little else, which is the cheapest structure of the three channels we cover.
items.label: Chatbot sessions
items.title: 24-hour sessions are unlimited and unbilled

items.body: A bot cannot message anyone who has not subscribed. For Business Messages Viber publishes no consent definition at all, so the standard is set by your aggregator and your regulator.
items.label: Opt-in
items.title: Platform-enforced for bots, contractual for Business Messages

items.body: A rejected template must be resubmitted under a new name. Template design is a release-planning problem, not a copywriting one.
items.label: Templates
items.title: Moderated by Viber, and immutable once submitted

items.body: Its terms apply controller-to-controller standard contractual clauses. The processor agreement you actually sign is your aggregator’s, and its sub-processor list is the one to read.
items.label: Data protection role
items.title: Viber is an independent controller, not your processor

head.heading: The constraints that decide *what you can actually build.*
head.lead: This is why WhatsApp is engineering work rather than a connector toggle. Every row below changes the design of the system. Verified against Meta’s WhatsApp Business Platform documentation in September 2026. Meta may change rates on 1 January, 1 April, 1 July or 1 October with one to six months’ notice depending on the change, so we date this panel and re-check it quarterly.

items.body: It resets on every inbound message. Outside it you may send only a pre-approved template, so your routing has to know how much window is left.
items.label: Messaging window
items.title: 24 hours from the customer’s last message or call

items.body: Both have been free since November 2024. Any quote built on the old model understates what the channel costs to run.
items.label: Pricing
items.title: From 1 October 2026, service messages and in-window utility templates become billable

items.body: Since April 2025 a utility template Meta judges to be marketing is approved as marketing rather than rejected, so you are billed at the higher rate with no error to catch.
items.label: Template categories
items.title: Marketing, utility and authentication, priced and policed differently

items.body: Shared across your whole business portfolio, not per number. Multi-brand groups hit the ceiling far earlier than they expect.
items.label: Messaging limits
items.title: 250 → 2,000 → 10,000 → 100,000 → unlimited unique recipients per rolling 24 hours

items.body: Direct means Meta bills you and the operational burden is yours. A Solution Partner holds the credit line and invoices you. We model both against your real volume.
items.label: Access model
items.title: Cloud API direct, or through a Solution Partner

items.body: Local storage covers Australia, India, Singapore, Japan, the UK and Germany among others. This is the answer to the residency objection most teams do not know exists.
items.label: Data residency
items.title: Pin data at rest to one country, or store nothing at rest at all

items.body: Meta relaxed the prescribed method, not the requirement. Your own regulator (GDPR, PDPA, India’s DPDP) sits on top, and it is usually the stricter one.
items.label: Opt-in
items.title: Required, and yours to evidence

items.body: If anything in your estate still points at it, those messages are not being delivered. Cloud API is the only remaining path.
items.label: On-Premises API
items.title: Expired 23 October 2025

head.heading: What this looks like in your industry

items.body: A buyer messages about a listing. The listing reference is parsed out of the message, the enquiry lands on the agent who owns that property, and the inspection booking writes straight back to the CRM, while the buyer stays in the app they started in.
items.label: Real estate
items.title: Enquiry to inspection without a spreadsheet in the middle

items.body: Appointment confirmations, reminders and check-in links as utility templates, with the conversation itself deliberately kept thin. Clinical content stays in the clinical system, because chat transcripts piped into a CRM turn into sensitive-data problems under PDPA and DPDP.
items.label: Healthcare
items.title: Bookings and reminders, without putting clinical detail in the thread

items.body: The ERP fires a delivery-window template the day before. The customer confirms or corrects the address by quick reply, and the reply carries the ID of the template that prompted it, which is how the correction gets back to the right consignment automatically.
items.label: Logistics
items.title: Address confirmation before the driver is already outside

items.body: Confirmation, dispatch and delivery updates sent as utility templates off the order record, with the reply landing in the same inbox your team already works from. Click-to-WhatsApp ads open a free 72-hour window, which is the economic reason they outperform.
items.label: Retail & ecommerce
items.title: Order status that does not generate a support ticket

items.body: Authentication and servicing notifications as templates, with residency pinned and consent evidenced. Note the hard limit: Meta prohibits several financial verticals outright, including payday loans and debt collection, whatever licences you hold.
items.label: Financial services
items.title: Servicing on the channel customers use, inside the rules you answer to

items.body: Prospective students answer on WhatsApp when they will not answer email. Enquiry, document chase and enrolment reminders run as templates against the student record, with the whole thread visible to whoever handles the application next.
items.label: Education
items.title: Enrolment follow-up that does not go to a dead inbox

head.heading: Why WhatsApp projects stall
head.lead: Four failure modes we are usually called in to undo, and what we do instead.

items.body: When they leave, the pipeline leaves with them. There is no reporting, no handover, and no record that a conversation ever happened.
items.title: It lives on someone’s personal phone

items.body: Submitted late, miscategorised as marketing, and suddenly the launch date belongs to Meta’s review queue rather than yours.
items.title: Templates written the night before launch

items.body: A checkbox on a form that never reached the CRM. The first regulator question is “show me”, and there is nothing to show.
items.title: Consent captured nowhere in particular

items.body: The marketplace app works for the pilot team, then the price to extend it to everyone else exceeds the cost of building it properly.
items.title: Per-seat app licences that cap the rollout

head.heading: How we build it

items.body: Registered to your portfolio, connected to the CRM, and reportable. People leave; the pipeline stays.
items.title: One business number, owned by the business

items.body: Written, categorised and submitted early, with the approval state monitored by webhook so a rejection is a task rather than a surprise.
items.title: Templates designed with the categories in mind

items.body: Captured at the point of opt-in with wording version and timestamp, honoured on and off WhatsApp, and exportable when someone asks.
items.title: Consent as a first-class field

items.body: Built against the Cloud API into your own system of record, with no per-seat licence between you and a full rollout.
items.title: An integration you own outright

head.heading: How the engagement *actually runs*
head.lead: Fixed phases, defined outcomes, published fees. You always know what is being delivered, by when, and at what cost.

items.body: Where conversations happen today, who owns them, what consent you can actually prove, and which access tier your volume justifies.
items.title: Channel & consent audit

items.body: How a message becomes a record, which object it attaches to, who it routes to, and what happens when nobody answers in time.
items.title: Data model & routing design

items.body: Rate limits, retries, dead-letter queues and alerting designed in, because integrations that fail silently corrupt trust in every connected system.
items.title: Build, with error handling first

items.body: Architecture documentation, a named maintenance path, and your team trained on the parts they will change. No mystery middleware.
items.title: Handover you can maintain
